content: Beta-ureidopropionase is an enzyme in humans that is encoded by the UPB1 gene. This gene produces a protein that is a member of the CN hydrolase family. Beta-ureidopropionase plays a critical role in the final step of the pyrimidine degradation pathway. In this pathway, the pyrimidine bases uracil and thymine are broken down through a sequential enzymatic process. This process involves the actions of dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase (DHPDH), dihydropyrimidinase (DHP), and beta-ureidopropionase (UP). These enzymes collectively degrade uracil and thymine into beta-alanine and beta-aminoisobutyric acid, respectively. Deficiencies in beta-ureidopropionase activity are associated with a condition known as N-carbamyl-beta-amino aciduria. This metabolic disorder can result in abnormalities in neurological function.
